_meta.what: Where prose leaves for a person, what field carries it, and who reads it there.
_meta.how_to_extend: Drop a file with the same shape at ~/.config/prose-guard/destinations.json. Your entries are tried BEFORE these, so you can override one as well as add one. Nothing here is required: a destination the tool does not recognise is simply not checked.
_meta.matching: tool matches if the string appears anywhere in the tool name, so MCP prefixes need not be spelled out. bash matches a regex against the command. file matches a regex against file_path.
_meta.audience_from: Names a field in the tool call. Its value's PREFIX is looked up in the map, longest prefix first, so a Slack channel id starting D means a direct message. Use '*' for the fallback.

D.audience: one colleague, in a direct message
D.shared_context: high: they are already in this conversation

C.audience: a whole channel of colleagues, most of whom lack your context
C.shared_context: low: readers arrive cold and out of order

G.shared_context: medium: they share some but not all of your context

when.thread_ts: a reply inside an existing thread, not a standalone message

*.reach: a private repository: colleagues can open internal links

audience_from.public_owners_note: List your public orgs under public_owners below to get the stronger warning.

audience.audience: colleagues reading documentation later, without you present
whoever picks this ticket up, possibly weeks from now
whoever reads this file later, without you present

when._edit: an edit to an existing document: judge the change, not the whole document

public_owners_help: Repository owners whose content outsiders can read. Listed here rather than guessed, because telling someone a private repo is public makes them strip links their colleagues could have opened.
